prompt: Match each commitment to what it is a commitment to.

pairs.right: One instance type in one region
Dollars an hour on one family in one region
Dollars an hour on EC2, Fargate and Lambda anywhere

prompt: What happens to the running instances when a Savings Plan is bought?

choices.text: They are moved to reserved hardware
choices.why: Nothing is reserved in the data centre.

choices.text: They are restarted on the new pricing
choices.why: No instance changes.

choices.text: They become protected from termination
choices.why: Billing does not change behaviour.

choices.text: Nothing; they run exactly as before
choices.why: Right. The bill applies a lower rate to covered hours.

prompt: Which commitment still applies after the shop moves its API from EC2 to Fargate?

choices.text: A standard RI for m7g.large
choices.why: It covers that EC2 type only.

choices.text: A Compute Savings Plan, which follows it
choices.why: Right. It follows the workload to Fargate and Lambda.

choices.text: An EC2 Instance Savings Plan for m7g
choices.why: It covers EC2 in one family.

choices.text: A convertible RI, once exchanged for Fargate
choices.why: RIs cannot be exchanged for Fargate.

prompt: In the rates table, how does the Compute Savings Plan's rate compare with the convertible RI's, term for term?
hint: Look at the pairs of lines.

choices.text: The same rate, term for term and payment for payment
choices.why: Right. The choice is about flexibility, not price.

choices.text: It is about 10 points cheaper
choices.why: The pairs are equal.

choices.text: It is dearer, since it is more flexible
choices.why: It matches the convertible RI exactly.

choices.text: It cannot be compared, since one is in dollars an hour
choices.why: Both resolve to a rate per instance-hour.

prompt: m7g.large costs 0.1301 USD an hour on demand and 0.0612 under a three-year all-upfront Compute plan. What is the discount, in percent? Round to the nearest whole number.
What moves the discount more for m7g.large: a longer term or paying upfront?

choices.text: Paying upfront, by about 20 points
choices.why: Upfront adds 5 points at most.

choices.text: Both move it equally
choices.why: 16 points against 5.

choices.text: Neither; only the instance family matters
choices.why: Both matter; the term matters more.

choices.text: The term, by about 16 points
choices.why: Right. One to three years moves 32% to 48% with no upfront.

prompt: rates.py spreads a reserved instance's upfront payment over the term's ____ to make every line comparable. (one word)
In commit.py's month, which commitment saved the most?
hint: The fewest that ever run at once.

choices.text: 8.8, the average
choices.why: Committing near the average left hours idle.

choices.text: 6, the fewest ever running at once
choices.why: Right. 22%, with nothing unused.

choices.text: 14, the working-hours level
choices.why: It cost more than all on demand.

choices.text: 18, the peak, so nothing is on demand
choices.why: Half the plan was unused: 39% worse.

prompt: A plan hour costs 0.0884 USD and replaces 0.1301 USD on demand. Above what share of the hours, in percent, must a committed instance be busy to pay for itself? Round to the nearest whole number.
The seventh instance in the shop's month runs about 45% of the hours. Why does the commitment stop at six?

choices.text: Six is a round number
choices.why: The number comes from the arithmetic.

choices.text: AWS sells plans in steps of six
choices.why: Plans are bought in dollars an hour, to the cent.

choices.text: 45% is under the 68% a plan hour needs
choices.why: Right. A seventh committed hour would cost more than it saves.

choices.text: The seventh is a different family
choices.why: All are m7g.large.

prompt: Why does a three-year plan justify a larger commitment than a one-year plan?

choices.text: Its break-even use is lower, 47%
choices.why: Right. A deeper discount pays off at lower use.

choices.text: It can be cancelled after a year
choices.why: It cannot be cancelled.

choices.text: Usage always grows over three years
choices.why: Not always; that is the risk.

choices.text: Three-year plans cover more services
choices.why: Coverage is the same for each kind.

prompt: A commitment shows 100% utilisation and 40% coverage. What does that say?
hint: Used fully, covering less than half.

choices.text: It is too large and partly wasted
choices.why: Full utilisation means nothing is wasted.

choices.text: The plan has expired
choices.why: An expired plan has no utilisation.

choices.text: Cost Explorer is misreporting
choices.why: It is a common and healthy state.

choices.text: It is safe and small
choices.why: Right. Nothing wasted, room to grow it.

prompt: Why rightsize before buying a commitment?

choices.text: Rightsizing raises the discount rate
choices.why: Rates do not depend on size choices.

choices.text: A commitment locks oversized instances in for the term
choices.why: Right. The waste is committed for one or three years.

choices.text: AWS refuses plans for oversized instances
choices.why: It sells them.

choices.text: Rightsizing is required by the RI Marketplace
choices.why: No such requirement.

prompt: What does the lesson take from moto's reserved instance offerings?

choices.text: A reason to take prices only from the price list
choices.why: Right. moto's prices are invented.

choices.text: The real prices, as of today
choices.why: They are made up, and change every run.

choices.text: The discount for sa-east-1
choices.why: They say nothing true about any region.

choices.text: The RI Marketplace listing
choices.why: moto has no marketplace.

prompt: Which of these does a commitment discount? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: EC2 instance hours
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Fargate, under a Compute plan
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Lambda, under a Compute plan
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Data transfer out
choices.why: Paid as before.

choices.text: S3 storage
choices.why: Paid as before.
